contentBlocks.text: Last week you studied world geography. This week: civic participation, the other half of this course's focus!

Civic participation means actively taking part in the life of your community and government, rather than just living passively within it — this can include voting, volunteering, attending public meetings, and staying informed about issues that affect your community. Democratic societies depend on people actually participating; a government structure alone doesn't guarantee a healthy democracy if citizens don't engage with it. List three different examples of civic participation, at least one of which doesn't involve voting.
You just learned what civic participation really means! Tomorrow we'll focus on voting specifically.

objectives: Define civic participation as actively engaging in community and government life
List three examples of civic participation, including at least one non-voting example
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review last week's world-geography work briefly.
2. Introduce civic participation and why democratic societies depend on it.
3. Have the child list three examples, including at least one non-voting example.
4. Complete the worksheet.
5. Preview tomorrow's voting-focused lesson.
differentiationTips: Struggling: offer a short list of examples (voting, volunteering, attending a town hall, writing to a representative) for the child to choose three from
Ready for more: ask the child why a government structure alone, without active citizen participation, might not be enough for a healthy democracy
Opens this week's civic-participation thread from the course's own description, distinct from last week's pure-geography focus
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is an open-ended activity — check that the child lists three genuine, distinct examples of civic participation and that at least one doesn't involve voting (e.g. volunteering, attending a public meeting, or contacting a representative).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses the C3 Framework's Civics dimension, opening this week's thread from the course's own description.
